verses.text: Now for di assembly wey dey Antioch, some prophets and teachers dey: Barnabas, Simeon wey dem dey call Niger, Lucius di Cyrenian, Manaen wey grow with Herod di tetrarch, and Saul.
As dem dey serve Lord and dey fast, Holy Spirit talk say, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for di work wey I don call dem to.”
Den, as dem don fast and pray and put dem hands on dem, dem send dem go.
So dem, as Holy Spirit send dem out, go down to Seleucia. From there dem sail go Cyprus.
When dem dey Salamis, dem proclaim God word for di synagogues of di Jews. John dey with dem as dem helper too.
When dem don pass through di island reach Paphos, dem find one sorcerer, false prophet, Jew wey im name na Bar Jesus,
wey dey with di proconsul, Sergius Paulus, man wey get understanding. Na im call Barnabas and Saul, dey want hear God word.
But Elymas di sorcerer—because na so im name mean—stand against dem, dey try turn di proconsul away from di faith.
But Saul, wey dem call Paul too, wey Holy Spirit full, fix im eyes on am,
and talk say, “You son of di devil, full of all deceit and all unrighteousness, you enemy of all righteousness, you no go stop to pervert di straight ways of di Lord?
Now, look, di hand of di Lord dey on you, and you go blind, no go see di sun for some time.” At once mist and darkness fall on am. E dey waka round dey look for person to lead am by di hand.
Den di proconsul, when e see wetin happen, believe, as di teaching of di Lord amaze am.
Now Paul and im group sail from Paphos, come reach Perga for Pamphylia. John leave dem return Jerusalem.
But dem, as dem pass from Perga, come reach Antioch of Pisidia. Dem enter di synagogue for Sabbath day, sit down.
After dem read di law and di prophets, di rulers of di synagogue send to dem, dey talk say, “Brothers, if una get any word of exhortation for di people, talk.”
Paul stand up, wave im hand, talk say, “Men of Israel, and una wey fear God, listen.
Di God of this people Israel choose our papa dem, and lift di people up when dem stay as strangers for di land of Egypt, and with raised arm, e lead dem out of am.
For about 40 years, e bear with dem for di wilderness.
When e don destroy seven nations for di land of Canaan, e give dem dem land as inheritance, for about 450 years.
After these things, e give dem judges until Samuel di prophet.
After, dem ask for king, and God give dem Saul, Kish son, man of di tribe of Benjamin, for 40 years.
When e remove am, e raise up David to be dem king, wey e give testimony and talk say, ‘I don find David, Jesse son, man after my heart, wey go do all my will.’
From this man seed, God don bring salvation to Israel according to im promise—Jesus.
Before im coming, John don first preach di baptism of repentance to all di people of Israel.
As John dey finish im course, e talk say, ‘Wetin una think say I be? I no be am. But look, one dey come after me wey I no worthy to loose di sandals of im feet.’
Brothers, pikin dem of Abraham stock, and di ones among una wey fear God, to us dem send out di word of this salvation.
Because di people wey dey live for Jerusalem, and dem rulers, because dem no recognize am, or di voices of di prophets wey dem dey read every Sabbath, dem fulfill dem as dem condemn am.
Though dem no find any reason for death, dem ask Pilate make dem kill am.
When dem don fulfill all things wey dem write about am, dem bring am down from di tree, put am for tomb.
But God raise am from di dead,
and many days people see am, di ones wey come up with am from Galilee to Jerusalem, wey be im witnesses to di people.
We dey bring una Good News of di promise wey dem make to di papa dem,
say God don fulfill di same to us, dem pikin dem, as e raise up Jesus. As e dey write for di second psalm too, ‘You be my Pikin. Today I don become your Papa.’
About say e raise am from di dead, now no more to return to corruption, e talk so: ‘I go give you di holy and sure blessings of David.’
So e talk for another psalm too, ‘You no go allow your Holy One see decay.’
Because David, after e don serve God plan for im own generation, sleep, dem put am with im papa dem, and e see decay.
But di one wey God raise up no see decay.
So make una know, brothers, say through this man dem dey proclaim forgiveness of sins to una,
and by am everybody wey believe dey justified from all things wey una no fit dey justified from by di law of Moses.
So beware, so that wetin dem talk for di prophets no go come on una:
‘Look, una scoffers, and marvel, and perish; because I dey do work for una days, work wey una no go believe at all, if person declare am to una.’”
As dem dey go out of di synagogue, di people beg make dem preach these words to dem di next Sabbath.
Now when di synagogue break up, many of di Jews and of di devout proselytes follow Paul and Barnabas; wey, as dem talk to dem, urge dem to continue for God grace.
Di next Sabbath, almost di whole city gather together to hear God word.
But di Jews, when dem see di crowds, jealousy full dem, and dem contradict di things wey Paul talk, and blaspheme.

Paul and Barnabas talk boldly, say, “E necessary say dem talk God word to una first. As una push am away from una, and judge yourselves unworthy of life wey no dey end, look, we dey turn to di Gentiles.
Because na so Lord command us, dey talk say, ‘I don set you as light for di Gentiles, so that you go bring salvation to di farthest parts of di earth.’”
As di Gentiles hear this, dem glad, and dem praise God word. As many as dem appoint to life wey no dey end believe.
Di word of di Lord spread through all di region.
But di Jews stir up di devout and prominent women and di chief men of di city, and stir up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and throw dem out of dem borders.
But dem shake off di dust of dem feet against dem, come Iconium.
Joy full di disciples with Holy Spirit.
E happen for Iconium say dem enter di synagogue of di Jews together, and talk so say great crowd of both Jews and Greeks believe.
But di Jews wey no believe stir up and make di Gentiles hearts bitter against di brothers.
So dem stay there long time, dey talk boldly for Lord, wey testify to di word of im grace, dey grant signs and wonders to happen by dem hands.
But di crowd of di city divide. Part join di Jews, and part join di apostles.
When some of both di Gentiles and di Jews, with dem rulers, try to mistreat and stone dem,
dem know am, run go di cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and di region round.
For there dem preach di Good News.
For Lystra one man dey sit, wey im feet no get power, cripple from im mama womb, wey never waka before.
E dey listen to Paul dey talk, wey fix im eyes on am, and see say e get faith to well,
talk with loud voice, “Stand up for your feet!” E jump up waka.
When di crowd see wetin Paul do, dem raise dem voice, dey talk for di language of Lycaonia, “Di gods don come down to us like men!”
Dem call Barnabas “Jupiter,” and Paul “Mercury,” because e be di chief speaker.
Di priest of Jupiter, wey im temple dey front of dem city, bring oxen and garlands to di gates, and e wan make sacrifice together with di crowds.
But when di apostles, Barnabas and Paul, hear am, dem tear dem clothes, rush enter among di crowd, dey shout

and dey talk say, “Men, why una dey do these things? We be men like una too, with di same feelings, and we dey bring una Good News, say una turn from these useless things to di living God, wey make di sky and di earth and di sea, and all wey dey inside dem;
wey for di generations wey don pass allow all di nations to waka for dem own ways.
Yet e no leave imself without witness, as e do good and give una rains from di sky and fruitful seasons, dey fill our hearts with food and gladness.”
Even as dem dey talk these things, dem hardly stop di crowds from making sacrifice to dem.
But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium come there, and as dem don persuade di crowds, dem stone Paul and drag am out of di city, dey think say e don die.
But as di disciples stand round am, e get up, enter di city. Di next day e go out with Barnabas go Derbe.
When dem don preach di Good News to that city, and make many disciples, dem return to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
dey strengthen di souls of di disciples, dey urge dem to continue for di faith, and say through many afflictions we must enter God Kingdom.
When dem don appoint elders for dem for every assembly, and don pray with fasting, dem commit dem to di Lord, wey dem believe.
Dem pass through Pisidia, come reach Pamphylia.
When dem don talk di word for Perga, dem go down to Attalia.
From there dem sail go Antioch, wia dem commit dem to di grace of God for di work wey dem don finish.
When dem reach, and gather di assembly together, dem report all di things wey God do with dem, and say e don open door of faith to di nations.
Dem stay there with di disciples for long time.
Some men come down from Judea teach di brothers, “Unless dem circumcise una after di custom of Moses, una no fit dey saved.”

So when Paul and Barnabas get no small disagreement and discussion with dem, dem appoint Paul and Barnabas, and some others of dem, to go up to Jerusalem to di apostles and elders about this question.
Dem, as di assembly send dem on dem way, pass through both Phoenicia and Samaria, dey declare di conversion of di Gentiles. Dem cause great joy to all di brothers.
When dem reach Jerusalem, di assembly and di apostles and di elders receive dem, and dem report everything wey God do with dem.
But some of di sect of di Pharisees wey believe get up, dey talk say, “E necessary to circumcise dem, and to command dem to keep di law of Moses.”
Di apostles and di elders gather together to look into this matter.

When plenty discussion don happen, Peter get up talk to dem say, “Brothers, una know say long time ago God make choice among una, say by my mouth di Gentiles go hear di word of di Good News, and believe.
God, wey know di heart, testify about dem, as e give dem Holy Spirit, just like e do to us.
E no make any distinction between us and dem, as e clean dem hearts by faith.
So now why una dey test God, say una put yoke on di neck of di disciples wey neither our papa dem nor we fit bear?
But we believe say we dey saved through di grace of Lord Jesus, just as dem dey.”
All di crowd keep quiet, and dem listen to Barnabas and Paul dey report wetin signs and wonders God don do among di Gentiles through dem.
After dem don quiet, James answer, “Brothers, listen to me.
Simeon don report how God first visit di Gentiles, to take from among dem people for im name.
This agree with di words of di prophets. As e dey write,
‘After these things I go return. I go build again di tabernacle of David, wey don fall. I go build again im ruins. I go set am up,
so that di rest of men go seek di Lord, and all di Gentiles wey dem call by my name, di Lord talk, wey dey do all these things.’
God don know all im works from eternity.
So my judgment na say make we no trouble di people from among di Gentiles wey turn to God,
but make we write to dem say make dem stay away from di pollution of idols, from sexual immorality, from wetin dem strangle, and from blood.
Because Moses from generations of old get for every city people wey dey preach am, as dem dey read am for di synagogues every Sabbath.”

Den e seem good to di apostles and di elders, with di whole assembly, to choose men from among dem, and send dem to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas wey dem call Barsabbas, and Silas, chief men among di brothers.
Dem write these things by dem hand: “Di apostles, di elders, and di brothers, to di brothers wey be of di Gentiles for Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
Because we don hear say some wey go out from among us don trouble una with words, dey upset una souls, dey talk say, ‘Una must dey circumcised and keep di law,’ wey we no give any commandment;
e seem good to us, as we don agree with one mind, to choose men and send dem to una with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
men wey don risk dem lives for di name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we don send Judas and Silas, wey go tell una di same things by word of mouth too.
Because e seem good to Holy Spirit, and to us, to put no greater burden on una than these necessary things:
say una stay away from things wey dem sacrifice to idols, from blood, from things wey dem strangle, and from sexual immorality; if una keep yourselves from these, e go well with una. Farewell.”
So, when dem send dem off, dem come Antioch; and as dem don gather di crowd together, dem deliver di letter.
When dem read am, dem rejoice over di encouragement.
Judas and Silas, as dem be prophets too, urge di brothers with many words and strengthen dem.
After dem don spend some time there, dem send dem back with greetings from di brothers to di apostles.
But e seem good to Silas to stay there.
But Paul and Barnabas stay for Antioch, dey teach and dey preach di word of di Lord, with many others too.
After some days Paul talk to Barnabas say, “Make we return now visit our brothers for every city wia we proclaim di word of di Lord, and see how dem dey.”
Barnabas plan to take John, wey dem call Mark, with dem too.
But Paul no think say e good to take with dem somebody wey leave dem for Pamphylia, and no go with dem to di work.
Den di argument become so sharp say dem separate from each other. Barnabas take Mark with am sail go Cyprus,
but Paul choose Silas and go out, as di brothers commit am to di grace of God.
E pass through Syria and Cilicia, dey strengthen di assemblies.
E come Derbe and Lystra: and look, one disciple dey there, wey im name na Timothy, son of one Jewish woman wey believe; but im papa na Greek.
Di brothers wey dey Lystra and Iconium give good testimony about am.
Paul want make e go out with am, and e take am circumcise am because of di Jews wey dey those parts, because dem all know say im papa na Greek.
As dem dey go di way through di cities, dem deliver di decrees to dem to keep, wey di apostles and elders wey dey Jerusalem don order.
So di assemblies strong for di faith, and dey increase for number every day.
When dem don pass through di region of Phrygia and Galatia, Holy Spirit forbid dem to talk di word for Asia.
When dem reach opposite Mysia, dem try to enter Bithynia, and di Spirit of Jesus no allow dem.
As dem pass Mysia, dem come down to Troas.
Vision appear to Paul for night. One man of Macedonia dey stand, dey beg am, dey talk say, “Come over enter Macedonia help us.”
When e see di vision, at once we try to go out to Macedonia, as we conclude say Lord don call us to preach di Good News to dem.
So as we sail from Troas, we go straight to Samothrace, and di next day to Neapolis;
and from there to Philippi, wey be city of Macedonia, di first of di district, Roman colony. We dey stay for this city some days.
For Sabbath day we go out of di city by one riverside, wia we think say place of prayer dey, and we sit down talk to di women wey gather.
One woman wey im name na Lydia, seller of purple, from di city of Thyatira, one wey worship God, hear us. Di Lord open im heart to listen to di things wey Paul talk.
When dem don baptize am and im household, e beg us, dey talk say, “If una don judge me to be faithful to di Lord, come enter my house stay.” So e persuade us.
E happen, as we dey go to prayer, say one girl wey get spirit of divination meet us, wey dey bring im masters plenty gain by fortune telling.
As e dey follow Paul and us, e shout, “These men na servants of di Most High God, wey dey proclaim to una di way of salvation!”
E do this for many days. But Paul, as e annoy well well, turn talk to di spirit say, “I command you for di name of Jesus Christ to come out of am!” E come out that very hour.
But when im masters see say di hope of dem gain don go, dem catch Paul and Silas, drag dem enter di marketplace before di rulers.
When dem bring dem to di magistrates, dem talk say, “These men, as Jews, dey disturb our city,
and dey set forth customs wey no dey lawful for us to accept or to observe, as we be Romans.”
Di crowd rise together against dem, and di magistrates tear dem clothes off dem, command say make dem beat dem with rods.
When dem don beat dem plenty, dem throw dem inside prison, order di jailer to keep dem safe;
wey, as e receive such command, throw dem into di inner prison, and fasten dem feet for stocks.
But about midnight Paul and Silas dey pray and dey sing hymns to God, and di prisoners dey listen to dem.
Suddenly big earthquake come, so that di foundations of di prison shake, and at once all di doors open, and everybody chains loose.
Di jailer, as e wake from sleep and see di prison doors open, draw im sword and dey about to kill imself, dey think say di prisoners don escape.
But Paul shout with loud voice, dey talk say, “No harm yourself, because we all dey here!”
E call for lights, rush enter, fall down dey tremble before Paul and Silas,
and bring dem out, talk say, “Oga dem, wetin I must do to dey saved?”
Dem talk say, “Believe Lord Jesus Christ, and you go dey saved, you and your household.”
Dem talk di word of di Lord to am, and to all wey dey im house.
E take dem that same hour of di night, wash dem stripes, and at once dem baptize am, e and all im household.
E bring dem up enter im house, put food before dem, and rejoice well well, with all im household, as e don believe God.
But when day break, di magistrates send di sergeants, dey talk say, “Let those men go.”
Di jailer report these words to Paul, dey talk say, “Di magistrates don send say make dem let una go. So now come out, go in peace.”
But Paul talk to dem say, “Dem don beat us publicly, without trial, men wey be Romans, and throw us inside prison. Dem dey release us secretly now? No, but make dem come demself bring us out.”
Di sergeants report these words to di magistrates, and dem fear when dem hear say dem be Romans,
and dem come beg dem. When dem don bring dem out, dem ask dem to leave di city.
Dem go out of di prison, enter Lydia house. When dem see di brothers, dem encourage dem, and leave.
Now when dem don pass through Amphipolis and Apollonia, dem reach Thessalonica, wia synagogue of di Jews dey.
Paul, as e dey do, enter go meet dem, and for three Sabbath days reason with dem from di Scriptures,
dey explain and dey show say Christ must suffer and rise again from di dead, and dey talk say, “This Jesus, wey I dey proclaim to una, na di Christ.”
Some of dem believe, and join Paul and Silas: from di devout Greeks great crowd, and from di chief women not few.
But di Jews wey no believe take some wicked men from di marketplace, and as dem gather crowd, dem set di city for uproar. As dem attack Jason house, dem dey try bring dem out to di people.
When dem no find dem, dem drag Jason and some brothers before di rulers of di city, dey shout, “These ones wey don turn di world upside down don come here too,
wey Jason don receive. These all dey act against di decrees of Caesar, dey talk say another king dey, Jesus.”
Di crowd and di rulers of di city trouble when dem hear these things.
When dem don take security from Jason and di rest, dem let dem go.
Di brothers at once send Paul and Silas away for night go Beroea. When dem reach, dem enter di Jewish synagogue.
Now these ones better pass those for Thessalonica, say dem receive di word with all readiness of mind, dey examine di Scriptures every day, to see whether these things na so.
Many of dem believe; and also Greek women of honorable estate, and many men.
But when di Jews of Thessalonica know say Paul don proclaim God word for Beroea too, dem come there too, dey stir up di crowds.
Den di brothers at once send Paul out to go reach di sea, and Silas and Timothy still stay there.
But di people wey escort Paul bring am reach Athens. As dem receive commandment for Silas and Timothy say make dem come to am very quick, dem leave.
Now while Paul dey wait for dem for Athens, im spirit vex inside am as e see say di city full of idols.
So e reason for di synagogue with di Jews and di devout people, and for di marketplace every day with di people wey dey there.

Some of di Epicurean and Stoic philosophers dey argue with am too. Some talk say, “Wetin this babbler want talk?” Others, “E seem like say e dey advocate foreign gods,” because e preach Jesus and di resurrection.
Dem hold am, bring am go di Areopagus, dey talk say, “We fit know wetin be this new teaching wey you dey talk?
Because you dey bring some strange things to our ears. So we want know wetin these things mean.”
Now all di Athenians and di strangers wey dey live there no spend dem time for anything else, except to tell or to hear some new thing.
Paul stand for middle of di Areopagus, talk say, “Una men of Athens, I see say una dey very religious for all things.

Because as I dey pass, and look di objects of una worship, I find altar too with this inscription: ‘To one god wey nobody know.’ So wetin una dey worship without knowing, na this I dey announce to una.
Di God wey make di world and all things inside am, e, as Lord of heaven and earth, no dey live for temples wey dem make with hands,
and men hands no dey serve am, as if e need anything, as e imself dey give all life and breath, and all things.
E make from one every nation of men to live on all di surface of di earth, as e don decide appointed seasons and di boundaries of dem dwellings,
so that dem go seek di Lord, if perhaps dem go reach out for am and find am, though e no far from each one of us.
‘Because inside am we dey live, and move, and get our being.’ As some of una own poets don talk, ‘Because we be im offspring too.’
As we be di offspring of God, we no suppose think say di Divine Nature be like gold, or silver, or stone, wey dem carve by art and design of man.
So God overlook di times of ignorance. But now e dey command say all men everywhere must repent,
because e don appoint one day wey e go judge di world for righteousness by di man wey e don appoint; wey e don give assurance to all men, as e raise am from di dead.”
Now when dem hear about di resurrection of di dead, some mock; but others talk say, “We want hear you again about this.”
So Paul go out from among dem.
But some men join am, and believe, among dem na Dionysius di Areopagite, and one woman wey im name na Damaris, and others with dem.
After these things Paul leave Athens, come Corinth.
E find one Jew wey im name na Aquila, man of Pontus by race, wey just come from Italy, with im wife Priscilla, because Claudius don command all di Jews to leave Rome. E come to dem,
and because e dey do di same trade, e stay with dem and work, because by trade dem be tent makers.
E reason for di synagogue every Sabbath, persuade Jews and Greeks.
But when Silas and Timothy come down from Macedonia, di Spirit press Paul, dey testify to di Jews say Jesus na di Christ.
When dem oppose am and blaspheme, e shake out im clothes talk to dem say, “Make una blood dey on una own heads! I clean. From now, I go go to di Gentiles!”
E leave there, enter di house of one man wey im name na Justus, one wey worship God, wey im house dey next door to di synagogue.
Crispus, di ruler of di synagogue, believe Lord with all im house. Many of di Corinthians, as dem hear, believe and dem baptize dem.
Lord talk to Paul for night by vision, “No fear, but talk and no keep quiet;
because I dey with you, and nobody go attack you to harm you, because I get many people for this city.”
E live there one year and six months, dey teach God word among dem.
But when Gallio na proconsul of Achaia, di Jews with one mind rise against Paul and bring am before di judgment seat,
dey talk say, “This man dey persuade men to worship God against di law.”
But when Paul dey about to open im mouth, Gallio talk to di Jews say, “If na matter of wrong or wicked crime, una Jews, e go make sense say I bear with una;
but if na questions about words and names and una own law, look am yourselves. I no want be judge of these matters.”
E drive dem from di judgment seat.
Den all di Greeks hold Sosthenes, di ruler of di synagogue, beat am before di judgment seat. Gallio no care about any of these things.
Paul, as e don stay many more days after this, take im leave of di brothers, sail from there go Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. E shave im head for Cenchreae, because e get vow.
E come Ephesus, and e leave dem there; but e imself enter di synagogue reason with di Jews.
When dem ask am to stay with dem longer time, e refuse;
but as e take im leave of dem, and talk say, “I must by all means keep this coming feast for Jerusalem, but I go return again to una if God want,” e sail from Ephesus.
When e land for Caesarea, e go up greet di assembly, and go down to Antioch.
As e don spend some time there, e leave, pass through di region of Galatia, and Phrygia, in order, dey strengthen all di disciples.
Now one Jew wey im name na Apollos, Alexandrian by race, eloquent man, come Ephesus. E mighty for di Scriptures.
This man don learn di way of di Lord. As e dey fervent for spirit, e talk and teach accurately di things about Jesus, though e know only di baptism of John.
E begin talk boldly for di synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila hear am, dem take am aside and explain di way of God to am more accurately.
When e decide to pass over enter Achaia, di brothers encourage am, and write to di disciples make dem receive am. When e come, e help plenty di people wey believe through grace;
because e powerfully defeat di Jews for argument, dey show publicly by di Scriptures say Jesus na di Christ.
